title: Cranberry Relish
description:
You can use either a grinder (an old fashioned meat grinder or a KitchenAid attachment) or a food processor to
grind up the relish. If you have it, use a grinder rather than a food processor because a grinder does a better
job smooshing the cranberries, orange, and apples together while it cuts them up. But either way will work.
ingredients: If you are using an old fashioned grinder, use the medium- sized grinder plate and set the grinder on the edge of a table with a large bowl or pan to catch the fruit mix as it is ground. Old fashioned grinders tend to leak juice down the grinder base, so you may want to set up a bowl underneath to catch the drips.

If you don't have an old fashioned grinder, you can use the grinder attachment to a KitchenAid mixer, or you can use a food processor. If you use a food processor, be careful not to over-pulse! Or you'll have mush instead of relish.
1 bag rinsed raw cranberries (maybe picked over a little for ones that are mushy)
1-2 apples, peeled and cored and cut into thick chunks
1-2 seedless oranges, peeled and cut into sections
1/3 to 1+ cups granulated sugar (depending on how sweet you would like your relish to be)
directions: Pulse the cranberries, orange sections, and apple chunks in the food processor. (Or, alternate the fruit as
you push it through grinder so that different fruits get ground together.)
Stir in the sugar. Start with less than 1/3 of a cup and keep adding bits until you reach your desired level of
Let sit at room temperature until the sugar dissolves, about 45 minutes. Store in the refrigerator until ready
